# Purpose of this overview

The purpose of this overview is to present a clear and complete summary of the datasets you will be analysing for your project, which is useful to identify and solve problems early on. Moreover, part of the results can be re-used for your final report. Note that results presented here are not necessarily final: you may still opt to perform modifications to your preprocessing pipeline, design (samples included) etc without the need to update this temporary overview. 

For this assignment we ask you to do the following:

- Present some general info on your datasets
- Present quality control (QC) on your raw sequencing files
- Load in the data and present the intensity/count/pseudocount data

If you prefer to align your sequencing data yourself (which is highly appreciated), you will already need to do so for this homework. However, since you already have to present QC results for the raw sequencing data, alignment is only a small additional effort (highly similar to what we performed in the practical session).

In order to complete this task you can find a R markdown template via Ufora and also a filled out example. Note that for the filled out example, datasets are not chosen around an matching topic, as should of course be the case for your project.

Note that in this overview, four types of experiments are presented (expression microarrays, methylation microarrays, RNA sequencing, and ChIP sequencing). For your project you only need to analyse two, so delete the sections you don't need.

# Methylation microarray data (Infinum)

## General info

Species: Homo Sapiens

Microarray type: Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation850 BeadChip

Samples: The dataset includes five ESCC samples and five matched adjacent normal tissue samples. 

## Intensity values

Read in your methylation data and display the head and dimensions of your beta and M values.

```{r}
#set the working directory
setwd("/Users/kimchaeyoung/Desktop/Applied_HT_analysis/Project")
dir <- "/Users/kimchaeyoung/Desktop/Applied_HT_analysis/Project/GSE157807_RAW"

# Load the Infinium data (.idat files)
fibromethyl_RG <-read.metharray.exp(dir, extended = TRUE, force = TRUE)
pheno <- read.table("phenotype_data.txt", header = T, sep = " ")

# Match the samplenames to the phenotypic sample IDs
sampleNames(fibromethyl_RG) <- substr(sampleNames(fibromethyl_RG), 1, 10)

# Add the phenotypic annotation
rownames(pheno) <- pheno$SampleID
pData(fibromethyl_RG) <- DataFrame(pheno)

# Subset the data
fibromethyl_RG <- fibromethyl_RG[, pData(fibromethyl_RG)$TissueType %in% c("ESCC", "NORMAL")]

# Change sample names to something more meaningful
sampleNames(fibromethyl_RG) <- paste(sampleNames(fibromethyl_RG), pData(fibromethyl_RG)$PatientID, sep = "_")

# Convert RGChannelSetExtended to MethylSet (nopreprocessing)
fibromethyl_raw <- preprocessRaw(fibromethyl_RG)

fibromethyl_raw

# Function to calculate M-values
getM <- function(Methylset, offset = 1){
  M <- log2((getMeth(Methylset)+offset)/(getUnmeth(Methylset)+offset))
  return(M)
}

# Take a look at the raw M- and beta-values
head(getBeta(fibromethyl_raw))
```

## (Pseudo)Count table

Read in your count data or your kallisto pseudocounts (via tximport) and display the head and dimensions of your (pseudo)count data object.

```{r}
# 필요한 라이브러리 로드

head(count_data)

# Extract the attributes of interest

  select(ensembl_id, gene_name)

head(tx2gene)

```
